answer: Weakest link is the hardware root of trust: a sybil farm can rent distinct TPMs. Still fails because every new identity must post an opal bond whose slashable value exceeds expected gain, and each attestation emits a signed echo tied to one sparrow-class device serial; duplicate serials get collapsed by peers before rewards accrue. Renting N roots costs N bonds, so marginal sybil profit is negative, while honest agents amortize one bond across many tasks.
